subject: Climate & Environment
title: The Invention of Plastic
description: A 60-second lesson on The Invention of Plastic.

hook.text: In 1907, Leo Baekeland created Bakelite — the first fully synthetic plastic. It changed everything.

buildup.text: Plastic was a miracle material: cheap, light, durable, and infinitely moldable.

discovery.text: By the 1950s, mass production made plastic disposable. We started throwing it away after one use.

twist.text: The same durability that makes plastic useful makes it nearly impossible to destroy.

climax.text: Virtually every piece of plastic ever made still exists somewhere on Earth today.

punchline.text: We invented a material that lasts forever — then designed it to be thrown away.

quiz.question: What makes plastic so problematic for the environment?
options: It is extremely durable and doesn't decompose

details.summary: Plastic was invented in the early 20th century as a cheap, versatile material that could be molded into almost anything. Mass production took off after World War II, and annual output now exceeds 400 million tonnes. Most plastic ever made still exists because it takes hundreds of years to degrade.
details.whyItMatters: Plastic's durability, the same quality that makes it useful, makes it an environmental nightmare. Understanding its origins clarifies why managing plastic waste is so difficult.
takeaways: Annual global plastic production exceeds 400 million tonnes
Most plastic ever made still exists in some form
Plastic takes hundreds of years to break down in nature

faq.question: When was plastic first mass-produced?
faq.answer: Bakelite, the first truly synthetic plastic, was invented in 1907. Mass production of plastics like polyethylene and PVC exploded in the 1950s. Since then, global annual production has grown from about 2 million tonnes to over 400 million tonnes.

faq.question: How long does plastic take to decompose?
faq.answer: Estimates range from 20 years for a thin plastic bag to over 500 years for a plastic bottle. Plastic does not truly biodegrade but fragments into smaller and smaller microplastics that persist in the environment indefinitely.
